metalone.title: Desktop metal printer (LPBF)
metalone.source: Sharebot MetalONE launch figures (740 x 630 x 1000 mm, 150 kg; 100 x 100 x 100 mm build; 200 W fibre laser), engineering.com, 3D Printing Industry, Fabbaloo; look from Sharebot's photos
notes: 1000 mm tall at launch (740 x 630 x 1000 mm, 150 kg); later listings give 1000 x 600 x 1470 mm and 270-315 kg, probably a stand or a bigger configuration.
Needs argon (or nitrogen for some alloys) and powder handling, which the VLM's trays don't have.

snowpod.title: Desktop metal printer (LPBF), pre-release
snowpod.source: 3DWithUs's review (360 x 360 x 660 mm, 40 kg, 200 W fibre laser); 3Dnatives and Makers101 (80 x 80 x 100 mm build, 40 um spot, sealed cartridges, NitroPod nitrogen); look approximate
notes: 360 x 360 x 660 mm and 40 kg are 3DWithUs's figures; SnowX's announcements give the build, the spot and the price but no outer size.
A Kickstarter kit, launch planned for Q4 2026 ($5,299 launch special, $9,299 MSRP), 316L only at launch: not shipping yet.
Nitrogen comes from SnowX's NitroPod, which makes it from air (99.9 % at 3 L/min), so on a tray it needs power, not a gas line. The NitroPod's size isn't published; it isn't modelled.
Powder stays in sealed supply and recovery cartridges; a cyclone, two H13 filters and an H14 at the exhaust.

mprint.title: Compact metal printer (LPBF)
mprint.source: One Click Metal MPRINT/MPRINT+ (1100 x 790 x 1900 mm, 440-450 kg; 150 mm cube build; 200 W fibre laser; five-cartridge powder revolver), filament2print, 3D Printing Industry, Autodesk; look from One Click Metal's photos
notes: The published figures are 1100 x 1900 x 790 mm (and 1.9 x 1.1 x 0.79 m); read as W x H x D from the photos, a 1.9 m cabinet.
Needs argon and depowdering in its separate MUNPACK station; check the supply rating with the maker.

meltio_m450.title: Compact wire-laser DED
meltio_m450.source: Meltio M450 technical specifications (560 x 600 x 1400 mm, 250 kg; 145 x 168 x 390 mm envelope; 6 x 200 W diode lasers at 976 nm; 0.8-1.2 mm wire); look from Meltio's photos
notes: The most compact DED found; Meltio's M600 is 1050 x 1050 x 1950 mm.
Needs argon and cooling, and 2-5 kW peak; wire feedstock means no loose powder.

form4.title: Resin 3D printer (MSLA)
form4.source: Formlabs Form 4 tech specs (398 x 367 x 554 mm, 18.3 kg; 407 x 478 x 844 mm with the cover open; 200 x 125 x 210 mm build volume); look from Formlabs' photos
notes: Fits a tray with 173.5 mm to spare under Kardex's 727.5 mm, but the cover opens to 844 mm: the arm can open it at the opening (about 845 mm under the header), never while the tray is in a slot
The cover's rear hinge is inferred from the published open envelope, not from a drawing

form_wash.title: Wash station for resin parts
form_wash.source: Formlabs Form Wash (2nd Gen): 315 x 293 x 405 mm, 714 mm tall with the lid open; look from Formlabs' photos
notes: Fits a tray closed (405 mm) and open (714 mm), under Kardex's 727.5 mm with 13.5 mm to spare
The bucket holds several litres of IPA: flammable vapour inside an enclosed VLM is a question for Kardex and EHS, as is the waste solvent

form_cure.title: Post-cure chamber, 405 nm and heat
form_cure.source: Formlabs Form Cure (2nd Gen): 337 x 356 x 404 mm, 12.1 kg, 405 nm light and heat, 235 mm turntable; look from Formlabs' photos and service guide
notes: Fits a tray with 323.5 mm to spare; the door swings out in front, so it opens at the opening
The door's hinge side is assumed; Formlabs' service guide confirms a door, not a lid

stencil.title: Solder paste stencil printer, semi-automatic
stencil.source: Pentalogix's SPR-45VA listing (762 x 889 x 406 mm, 584 mm frames); DDM Novastar's SPR-45 description (160 lb, dual squeegees, power frame lift); layout from resellers' photos
stencil.where: on a VLM tray, turned 90 deg
notes: The layout between the published outline is generic for a benchtop semi-automatic printer.
Semi-automatic: someone, or the arm, puts the board on the nest and takes it off; the machine aligns, prints and separates.
889 mm deep against the tray's 840, so it goes on the tray turned 90 degrees.
Solder paste lives in a fridge and needs time to warm up; the paste on the stencil dries out over a few hours, so someone has to wipe the stencil.

lumenpnp.title: Pick-and-place, open source
lumenpnp.source: Opulo's LumenPnP repository (DESIGN_DECISIONS.md, bom.json: 600 mm V-slot, two nozzles, top and bottom vision, 120 x 600 mm staging plates, boards to 225 x 400 mm) and its v4 photo; overall size estimated from the extrusions and the photo
notes: Opulo publishes no overall size; 680 x 680 x 450 mm is the 600 mm extrusions plus the legs, and the height scaled from Opulo's photo (about +-15 %).
Open hardware: the CAD is FreeCAD and the firmware is Marlin, driven by OpenPnP.
It needs no compressed air: its vacuum pumps are on board.
